scenario.name: Cisco Talos — ArcaneDoor (UAT4356): Cisco ASA Zero-Days, Line Dancer & Line Runner
scenario.shortSubtitle: Cisco Talos · CVE-2024-20353 / CVE-2024-20359, host-scan-reply Shellcode & Syslog Disable
scenario.overview: A fortress gatekeeper checks visitor clearance cards using an internal handbook kept on a live workbench. An outsider slips a coded message into the clearance envelope that rewrites pages on the live workbench, turns off the watchtower alarm bell, and plants a hidden archive package in the basement vault so the backdoor returns after every seasonal rebuild. In this scenario (CVE-2024-20353, Cisco Talos, ArcaneDoor (UAT4356): Cisco ASA Zero-Days, Line Dancer & Line Runner), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: delivering Base64-Encoded Shellcode Payloads, then "Line Dancer" In-Memory Implant Disables, then "Line Runner" Abuses vpn_dessert.zip. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Delivering Base64-Encoded Shellcode Payloads, then "Line Dancer" In-Memory Implant Disables, then "Line Runner" Abuses vpn_dessert.zip, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: ASA ZERO-DAY EXPLOIT & LINE RUNNER FLASH PERSISTENCE
stages.subtitle: Chaining CVE-2024-20353 & CVE-2024-20359 to persist on disk0:
stages.description: An uninvited courier mails an oversized clearance envelope to the fortress side window. Inside the reply form, folded rows of coded symbols slip past the gatekeeper check and place raw instructions onto the active guard workbench. To control the compromised Cisco ASA firewall without opening any suspicious new network port, the attacker sends standard HTTPS POST requests on port 443 to /CSCOSSLC/config-auth (the exact URL that every remote employee’s Cisco AnyConnect VPN client connects to every morning, allowing the attacker’s command-and-control traffic to blend seamlessly into legitimate corporate VPN logins). Inside the XML body’s <host-scan-reply> tag, the attacker places a 32-byte magic identifier followed by a Base64-encoded shellcode command. Normally, the ASA’s XML parser processes <host-scan-reply> during AnyConnect posture checks. Because the Line Dancer hook intercepts the buffer inside the lina process as soon as it spots the 32-byte magic header (before standard VPN authentication even finishes), the attacker can send commands without needing a valid VPN username or password. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ LINE RUNNER BOOT / ⇠#1 ACK CVE-2024-20359) from Node ① (#1 UAT4356 (Storm-1849) Actor) to Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cisco Talos / NetFlow SIEM).

stages.title: LINE DANCER IN-MEMORY SHELLCODE INTERPRETER
stages.subtitle: Hooking SSL VPN <host-scan-reply> inside /asa/bin/lina
stages.description: Once active on the workbench, a silent in-memory agent mutes the watchtower logbook bell and redirects incoming check-in packets so the outsider can inspect traffic and run custom gate commands without leaving paper records. Inside the ASA’s main lina executable (the monolithic process that handles all firewalling, routing, and VPN sessions on a Cisco ASA), the Line Dancer memory-only implant decodes the incoming shellcode and executes it directly in RAM. Before running reconnaissance or capturing packets, Line Dancer patches the in-memory syslog logging function (temporarily silencing outbound syslog alerts so the SOC’s SIEM server never sees that someone just ran "show running-config" or started a packet capture) and disables crash dumps (so if an exploit attempt crashes a thread, no forensic core dump is written to disk). Because perimeter network appliances cannot run standard Windows/Linux EDR agents, modifying the running lina process in volatile RAM hides the implant from normal CLI checks, and can only be caught on-box by hashing the live memory text segment via verify /md5 system:memory/text. In the documented HTTPS POST scan.xml exchange from DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap to Cisco ASA 5500-X Firewall, Cisco ASA 5500-X Firewall responds with RESP 1,420 Bytes (confirming that the LINE DANCER C2 request succeeded on Cisco ASA 5500-X Firewall and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 SYSLOG SUPPRESSION, PCAP CAPTURE & CONFIG EXFIL). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ LINE DANCER C2 / ⇠#2 RESP 1,420 Bytes) from Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Cisco ASA 5500-X Firewall), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cisco Talos / NetFlow SIEM).

Because Line Dancer lives purely in RAM, rebooting the firewall would normally wipe it out. Combining Line Runner (disk0: boot persistence via CVE-2024-20359) with Line Dancer (volatile RAM command execution inside lina) gives the attacker both reboot survival and zero-footprint daily operation. detectionRule.title: Cisco Talos — ArcaneDoor Line Runner Lua Webshell Backdoor
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule CiscoTalos_ArcaneDoor_LineRunner {
  meta:
    author = "Cisco Talos Intelligence Group"
    campaign = "ArcaneDoor (UAT4356)"
  strings:
    $s1 = "csco_config.lua" ascii
    $s2 = "os.execute" ascii
    $s3 = "HTTP_X_CSCO_" ascii
  condition:
    all of them
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Upgrade Cisco ASA/FTD software to patched releases fixing CVE-2024-20353 and CVE-2024-20359 and inspect disk0: for unauthorized .zip files.

detectionRule.title: Cisco ASA Syslog Telemetry Silence or Memory Integrity Alert
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Cisco ASA Logging Disabled or Memory Verification Failure
logsource:
  product: cisco
  service: asa
detection:
  selection:
    Message|contains:
      - 'Logging disabled'
      - 'Error verifying system:memory/text'
      - '%ASA-5-111008'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Alert on any gap in perimeter firewall syslog heartbeats (>5 minutes) and schedule automated "verify /sha-512 system:memory/text" integrity checks.
